evals.prompt: Our indie bookshop's plan for next year is the usual: more author events, a loyalty card, and pushing online orders through our website. It all feels safe and a bit dead. Make some trouble — throw crazy provocations at it, find anything usable, then tell me honestly whether the new stuff or our current plan is more likely to fail.
evals.expected_output: A Troublemaker's report showing which labelled provocations moved and the 1–3 concrete ideas they became, a side-by-side pre-mortem of the strongest idea versus the current plan (events, loyalty card, online orders) with kill/wound/scratch severities and hardening moves, a switch/hybrid/stay verdict, a first piece of trouble, and a Handoff block.
expectations: The three agents think-troublemaker-provocateur, think-troublemaker-movement-miner, and think-troublemaker-red-teamer were each spawned, in that order, each only after the previous one returned

The provocateur's list has 10–15 provocations, each labelled with a technique, spanning at least four distinct techniques, with no evaluative commentary such as 'impractical' or 'could work if' attached
Every mined idea names the provocation and movement technique it came from, and at least one provocation is explicitly marked barren

The pre-mortem attacks both the strongest mined idea and the stated plan (author events, loyalty card, online orders), grading each failure kill, wound, or scratch and pairing each with a hardening move
The final output ends with a '## Handoff' section

evals.prompt: We're migrating our monolith to microservices over the next 12 months — the plan's approved and the team is excited. Play devil's advocate and poke holes in it, but also give me some genuinely lateral alternatives so it's not just negativity.
evals.expected_output: Provocations aimed at the migration's taken-for-granted assumptions, concrete ideas mined from them, and a symmetric pre-mortem in which the approved microservices migration is the status quo attacked on the same kill/wound/scratch scale as the strongest alternative, ending in a switch/hybrid/stay verdict with hardening moves.
expectations: The red-teamer treats the approved microservices migration as the status-quo plan and attacks it on the same kill/wound/scratch scale as the strongest mined idea
At least one status-quo failure is a slow or quiet one (e.g. the migration dragging on, opportunity cost, eroding delivery speed), not only a dramatic outage
The provocations include at least one exaggeration (×1000 or ÷1000) and at least one escape that removes something taken for granted about the system or the migration
Mined ideas are concrete moves stating who does what differently, not restatements of the provocations
The final verdict states switch, hybrid, or stay and names the hardening moves that make the chosen path survivable
